reason: This is the only offered combination, and supplying the muscle fibers should support their continuing work.

reason: This is the only offered combination, and wrapping the fibers seems like a step toward organizing them into a muscle.

effect: The wrapping organizes muscle fibers into bundles and helps pass their tension toward the muscle's ends. I can now attach tendons to prepare a pull.
reaction: The explanation connects the cells' work to the structure of a muscle clearly.
reason: I'll attach the front tendons first to prepare one side of the arm; either side seems reasonable.
expectation: I expect a front muscle assembly that can connect to the arm framework, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons also need attaching, but I have no particular reason to prefer that side first.

reaction: The link between tendon position and the direction of movement is clear.
reason: I'll fit the bending muscles into the framework to complete the front pull.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to fill the framework's front-pull slot.

alternatives.reason: I also considered preparing the rear pull first, but the front assembly is ready to fit.

reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the two-sided muscle arrangement.

effect: The completed framework can bend, straighten and steady the elbow through opposing pulls, including pulling while holding a weight still. Coordination remains a separate job.
reaction: Holding a weight without the muscles shortening was an interesting extension of the model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bending muscles was worthwhile because it connected the muscle's pull through tendons to movement at the joint and explained why relaxing cannot push the arm back.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining oxygen with partly processed fuel felt predictable, although the result clarified oxygen's role.

surprise.text: I found it useful that sugar breakdown makes some ATP in the cell fluid before mitochondria use the partly processed fuel.

arbitrary.text: Choosing the front tendons before the rear tendons felt arbitrary because either side seemed equally reasonable to prepare first.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the opposing muscles are coordinated; the connections from cellular fuel use to the arm's movement held my interest, though many steps were predictable.
